cues: Behind hinged wooden doors, adjustable horizontal supports keep reference volumes upright and shield their spines from dust.
Divided compartments fit dictionaries and novels, with broad interior boards bearing their weight across sturdy side panels.
Glass-fronted timber furniture displays hardbacks while protecting their covers from dust and handling.
Vertical partitions and flat crosspieces form orderly bays for atlases, dictionaries, and other heavy volumes.
Reinforced joints keep the tall wooden structure stable when densely packed reference books load its lower sections.
Removable interior boards accommodate changing book sizes inside a deep, paneled storage frame.
Matching doors conceal spare volumes, while narrow upper compartments keep frequently used paperbacks within reach.
A broad base and braced sides prevent rows of heavy encyclopedias from making the storage unit wobble.
